title: Institute of American Civics - Open Rank Tenure Track Professor in American Civics Fall 2027
description:
Description

The Institute of American Civics, located within the Howard H.
Baker, Jr. School of Public Policy and Public Affairs at the
University of Tennessee, Knoxville, is seeking to fill a
tenure-line 9-month faculty position at the assistant through full
professor rank in American Civics to begin August 1, 2027.

Successful candidates will be expected to teach undergraduate
classes on a 2-2 load and carry out a program of research and
scholarship. They will also be expected to be actively engaged in
the Institute’s activities.

Who We Are

The I nstitute of American Civics was created to enhance education
in politics, economics, philosophy, American history, and American
government as well as increase understanding of the rights and
responsibilities of American citizenship; fundamental democratic
principles; and the ways in which those principles are expressed in
and through our federal, state, and local institutions. In pursuit
of this mission, the Institute invites applications from scholars
at all ranks with teaching and research profiles in American
political thought and American political institutions (including
federalism). Additional interests in ancient to early modern
political philosophy and/or political economy are desirable.
Willingness to engage in student programming and public outreach is
also required.

The Baker School was established in 2023 to honor the distinguished
life and legacy of Howard H. Baker Jr., a former US Senator, Senate
Majority Leader, White House Chief of Staff, and Ambassador to
Japan. The Baker School evolved from the Baker Center, which
produced research, public engagement programming, and an active set
of student programs for twenty years. The Baker School has now
added degree programs and grown its research programming into
several independent research centers.

We are a dynamic and close-knit team of dedicated and hardworking
individuals who are devoted to our mission of research, education,
and public service initiatives, and are dedicated to moving the
Baker School forward.

The University of Tennessee, Knoxville, is the state’s flagship
research institution, a campus of choice for outstanding
undergraduates, and a premier graduate institution. As a land-grant
university, it is committed to excellence in learning, scholarship,
and engagement with society.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications Candidates must possess a PhD
in political science, history, economics or a related discipline at
the time of appointment (August 1, 2027).

Rank-Specific Qualifications Assistant Professor:
Candidates should have a demonstrated potential for publishing in
appropriate venues, including a strong Ph.D. dissertation which has
been published in some form or for which the candidate has a viable
strategy for publication, and exceptional teaching. Advanced
candidates for Assistant Professor should have a record of actual
publications, and should show development of a trajectory that goes
beyond the dissertation.

Associate Professor: Candidates should have a demonstrated record
of publishing in appropriate venues, exceptional teaching, and
internal and external service to their professional
community.

Full Professor: Candidates should have a demonstrated record of
publishing in appropriate venues, exceptional teaching, and
internal and external service to their professional community. In
addition, the candidate should have national/international
recognition in their field of study.

Appropriate venues can include books, journal articles, and
contributions to edited volumes. Some demonstrated capacity to
attract external grant or fellowship funding is a plus.

Application Instructions

Applicants should send a cover letter explaining their research,
teaching experience, record of service (if any), commitment to the
Institute’s mission, and which IAC courses they are prepared to
teach. They should also send a current CV, a research statement, a
sample of scholarly writing, and recent student teaching
evaluations (if available). All applicants should provide a list of
references.

Applicants should submit the following via Interfolio:

-CV

-Cover Letter

-List of three references with contact information

-Research Statement

-Sample of scholarly writing

-Student Evaluations if available.

Successful candidates will be required to submit official
transcripts and undergo a background check. Screening of applicants
will begin on September 1, 2026, and will continue until the
position is filled. For questions or inquiries, contact the search
chair: Dr. Andrew Busch, abusch1@utk.edu .
